clue.text: Skilful strings play in tennis match (first class!)

parts.note: a tennis match between pairs is a game of doubles
topping is old-fashioned British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A violinist shows dazzling technique during a top-quality tennis game.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed exclamation reads as applause for the match, but it is just the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Double stopping is the violin technique of bowing two strings at once, a skilful way of playing.

clue.text: Dejected after plucking birds with one's teeth?

definitions.text: after plucking birds with one's teeth
definitions.meaning: second, playful meaning: feathers pulled off with the teeth end up between one's lips

explanation.walkthrough: Down is the soft feather of a bird, so someone plucking with their teeth has it, literally, in their mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a miserable, unhappy expression, the corners of the lips turned low.

clue.text: Ideally perfect note on new piano

parts.note: ut is the old name for the first note of the scale, now do

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the following word's letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone praises a brand-new piano, playing a note on it that sounds flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined perfect society, so a utopian plan is idealistic and flawless.

clue.text: Gladly permit to remain uncultivated

parts.note: lief is an archaic word for gladly, as in 'I'd as lief'
to permit is to allow

explanation.surface: A farmer happily agrees to let a field rest unplanted for a season.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that lies fallow is left unplanted for a season, so it stays unworked.

clue.text: Oliver, for example, getting Ruth to relent

parts.note: Oliver! is a stage musical, an example of a show
ruth is an old word for compassion, as in ruthless

explanation.surface: A boy called Oliver persuades a girl called Ruth to give in.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver and Ruth look like two people's names; one is a musical and the other a lowercase noun meaning compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften and let mercy win, which is what showing compassion means.

clue.text: State alternative to Ronay

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
Egon Ronay was a well-known British restaurant critic and guide writer

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to name another food critic instead of Ronay.
explanation.walkthrough: Egon Ronay published famous restaurant guides in Britain, so his first name is what goes with his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is one of the fifty United States, on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Tree with flat surface

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a broad-leaved tree common in city streets
second meaning: a level two-dimensional surface in geometry

explanation.surface: A tree is described as having a level face.
explanation.definitionFit: The London plane is a familiar tree, and in geometry a plane is a perfectly level surface.

clue.text: Boy taking novice a flower

parts.note: a boy's name
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lad brings a beginner a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella, love-in-a-mist, is a garden plant grown for its blue blooms.

clue.text: Its report should stimulate athletic progress

definitions.text: Its report should stimulate athletic progress

parts.words: Its report should stimulate athletic progress
parts.note: surface reading: a written report on an athlete meant to spur improvement
setter's reading: a report is the bang of a gun, which sends runners off down the track

explanation.walkthrough: Report sounds like a document; here it is the noise of a shot fired at the start of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The gun fired to begin a race makes a bang that sets the runners moving forward.

clue.text: Unbroken part is healthy

parts.note: unbroken means intact, entire
some means a portion of something

explanation.surface: A paradoxical claim that the intact piece is the fit one.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesome food or living is good for you and promotes wellbeing.

clue.text: Try to acquire outward skill in slang

indicators.note: the attempt acquires the following word around it, so that word sits outside

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of conversation
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Advice to pick up a knack for street talk from the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the private jargon or cant of a particular group, a form of slang.

clue.text: Excerpt from Nazi bible put back in place

indicators.note: putting it back means running the extracted letters in the opposite direction
an excerpt is a piece lifted out of a longer text, here out of the next two words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A passage from a Nazi text is restored to its proper position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back in place' reads as one phrase, but 'place' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish Balearic island and holiday resort, a geographical location.

clue.text: Appropriate length in a driving mechanism

indicators.note: one word is placed inside another, so the measure sits within the adjective

parts.note: appropriate means fitting, suitable
an ell is an old cloth measure of length

explanation.surface: A sensible distance is called for in some motoring part.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw with blades turns to push a ship or aircraft forward, so it drives the craft.

clue.text: Not returning to Italy, perhaps, for key

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the country name is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller decides against going back to Italy, maybe for some important reason.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the key of a piece is its tonality, the system of notes centred on one tonic.

clue.text: Expedition to see sporting body in foreign attire

indicators.note: the sports organisation is dressed in the garment, placed inside it

parts.note: a sari is the draped garment worn by women in South Asia
the FA is the Football Association, which runs English football

explanation.surface: Football officials travel abroad in exotic dress to watch wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is a journey or expedition, especially one to observe or hunt African animals.

clue.text: Citadel producing a harvest on poor soil

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the earth word's letters are broken up and reordered

parts.note: a crop is what is harvested
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fortress somehow yields a crop from barren ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is the fortified upper part of an ancient Greek city, like the one in Athens.

clue.text: He hopes to make a profit from vines replanted on hill

definitions.text: He hopes to make a profit

indicators.note: plants moved to new positions suggest the letters being set down in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: A wine grower expects good returns after moving the grapevines up a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts money into a venture does so expecting a financial return.

clue.text: Makes financial provision on getting bad news about party

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled word goes around the celebration
bad suggests something spoilt, so the letters of the report word are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone hears unwelcome tidings about a political party and arranges their finances.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give a lasting fund or income, such as money settled on a college.

clue.text: One who straightens furniture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who dresses, lining up troops or ranks straight
second meaning: a kitchen sideboard with shelves for plates

explanation.surface: A tidy person puts the furniture in order.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers dress ranks by lining them up, so one who dresses straightens.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is a cupboard with open shelves above, and also anyone who dresses or aligns things.

clue.text: Unusually daring, if demeaning

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the following letters are arranged in an uncommon order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bold act that is rather undignified.
explanation.definitionFit: From Latin infra dignitatem, the phrase means beneath one's dignity, hence degrading.

clue.text: Hollow tear produced by certain flies

parts.note: a dip is a hollow in the ground

indicators.note: produced suggests something made anew, so the letters of the crying word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An empty teardrop caused by some insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Diptera is the insect order of two-winged flies, including houseflies and mosquitoes.

clue.text: Object when time signal is put out for birds

indicators.note: the signal is put outside, set around the thing instead of within it

parts.note: the pips are the beeps broadcast on BBC radio to mark the hour
it is a pronoun standing for an object

explanation.surface: Someone protests when a radio time signal is broadcast for the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Object reads as a verb, to protest, but it is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipits are small brown songbirds of open country, such as the meadow pipit.

clue.text: Labourer having the power to act

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a worker, especially in a factory

explanation.surface: A worker is described as having authority to take action.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a factory hand, and a rule that is operative is in effect and working.

clue.text: Confound with a blow

parts.note: taken as written
a bash is a heavy blow

explanation.surface: Someone is knocked senseless by a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to embarrass or disconcert someone, leaving them confused and flustered.

clue.text: Is to go back for a drink

indicators.note: going back means the joined words are then read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
go means energy or vigour, as does pep

explanation.surface: Someone is returning home for a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go back' reads as a phrasal verb, but go is a noun meaning get-up-and-go.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepsi is a well-known brand of cola soft drink.

clue.text: Girl bringing back something worth having

indicators.note: bringing it back means returning along the word from its end

parts.note: an asset is something valuable or useful

explanation.surface: A young woman returns with something valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: Tessa is a female first name, short for Theresa.

clue.text: Let client exercise rational powers

indicators.note: exercise puts something through movements, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer lets the customer use their own reason.
explanation.definitionFit: The intellect is the mind's capacity for reasoning and understanding.

clue.text: Cart-horse conducted to stable in theatre

definitions.note: describes where the seat is rather than naming it

indicators.note: conducted means led somewhere else, so the hyphenated phrase's letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a stall is a stable compartment for one animal

explanation.surface: A dray horse is led to its stable inside a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Conducted points at an orchestra on the surface too, a neat touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestra stalls are the seats on the ground floor near the stage of a British playhouse.
